rows.body: The answer comes before the whole question.

A long discussion becomes a yes or no when someone asks the direct question. Mercury in Aries answers quickly, states the point plainly, and may decide from the first useful fact before the remaining information arrives.

Until {{exitDate}}, a message with two questions gets an immediate answer to the first, while the second goes unnoticed. In a meeting, someone names the point directly and the group reaches a decision. A slower explanation gets interrupted, then repeated when one missing detail changes the plan. Instructions get skimmed, the task begins, and an overlooked step has to be done again.

The same speed that ends a delay can create another one. A direct answer saves time when the information is complete. When it is not, the decision has to be reopened and the interrupted explanation has to start again.
A careful answer can still become outdated.

The conversation slows until there is a clear answer. Mercury in Taurus makes people wait before responding and check new information against what has already worked, but a familiar conclusion may remain after the facts supporting it change.

Until {{exitDate}}, a message gets reread before a firm answer is sent. Someone asks what a revised plan will change before agreeing to it. A point gets repeated in a meeting until everyone understands what was decided. A new detail is acknowledged, but the original decision stays in place.
Taking time can prevent a rushed decision, but treating a familiar answer as proof that nothing needs to change can keep an outdated plan in place.
The next question arrives before the current answer is finished.
Mercury in Gemini turns one answer into three more questions. It makes separate facts easier to connect, and a complicated point may become clear while it is being explained.

Until {{exitDate}}, someone changes an opinion when new information arrives and can explain exactly what changed. Two comments made at different points in a meeting reveal a connection that had been missed. A message leads to a useful source, then that source raises another question. The original reply remains unfinished while attention moves to the newest information.
Moving between several sources helps reveal connections, but it also divides attention, so a conclusion may be repeated before the reasoning behind it is complete.
The message is new. The reaction may not be.

A shorter reply, a longer pause, or one familiar phrase can change how the whole conversation is understood. Mercury in Cancer remembers what was said before and listens for what the current words may be leaving out.

Until {{exitDate}}, a short reply sends someone back through the messages that came before it. Someone remembers how a similar conversation ended and delays answering until the tone becomes clearer. In a meeting, one story explains why a decision matters, while a past disagreement shapes the response before anyone confirms that the same problem is happening.

Memory can supply useful context, but it is not always current evidence. The same attention that catches a real change in tone can make a neutral message sound like the last difficult one. The reply then addresses an earlier conversation instead of the words on the screen.
The point is memorable. The disagreement gets personal.

A confident explanation can make a complicated idea easy to follow. Mercury in Leo brings the speaker's point of view into the message, so criticism of the idea can sound like criticism of the person who shared it.

Until {{exitDate}}, someone tells a story with enough emphasis that its main point sticks. A plan is presented with confidence, and the explanation makes clear why the decision matters. A correction in front of others can turn a discussion of the facts into a defense of the person who spoke.

Conviction makes the message easier to remember, but pride can pull the exchange away from the original question. Once disagreement feels personal, proving the speaker was right can matter more than checking the facts.
Careful checking catches the error, but it can also delay the answer.

Mercury in Virgo notices the missing detail, the unclear instruction, and the claim that does not hold up when checked. That precision makes information more useful, but it can also keep a clear message unsent through one more round of edits.

Until {{exitDate}}, someone catches an error before it gets repeated and rewrites an explanation so the next person can follow it. A question in a meeting reveals that the plan depends on a detail nobody has confirmed. Elsewhere, a decision waits while the same facts are checked again, and the delay leaves people working from a guess.
The same scrutiny that catches the mistake can become another reason not to decide. An imperfect answer sent on time can be corrected; a late answer may leave the wrong version in circulation.
Everyone gets heard, but the first proposal may still become the plan.

The wording changes, and a disagreement that kept stalling can finally continue. Mercury in Libra compares two accounts and asks who has been giving up more, but a preference may not be stated until everyone else has weighed in.

Until {{exitDate}}, messages get revised so the point can be heard instead of dismissed. A meeting pauses because two people remember the same agreement differently, and both accounts are checked before the next step is chosen. A plan that sounded fair gets questioned when one person is always the one changing their schedule. By the time everyone has had a say, the first proposal may already have become the plan.

Comparing accounts can correct a decision based on only one version of events. Waiting for agreement before stating a position can also let the first or loudest speaker set the terms. A point softened enough to please everyone may no longer say what its speaker meant.
One missing detail can undo an explanation, but suspicion can continue after the necessary facts are known.

Mercury in Scorpio notices when one detail does not match the explanation. The question no one has asked becomes harder to avoid, and each answer gets checked against earlier messages before anyone relies on it.

Until {{exitDate}}, someone checks an answer against an earlier message, finds that the two do not match, and postpones a decision. In a meeting, a direct question brings a withheld fact into the discussion. An incomplete answer can also stall a plan when it is treated as proof that more is being hidden, even after the useful facts are available.

Looking past the first answer can uncover the fact a decision depends on, but suspicion can keep the decision on hold after the available information is enough. When one person controls when a relevant fact can be discussed, everyone else must either wait or act without it.
The larger point sounds settled before the details are checked.

A complicated discussion finally moves when the larger point is stated plainly. Mercury in Sagittarius connects scattered facts to a broader conclusion, making the idea easier to explain and repeat. The same confidence can make a claim sound complete before its supporting details are checked.

Until {{exitDate}}, a meeting can move forward when someone explains what several updates add up to. A message gives the reason behind a decision, and the plan becomes easier to understand. One detail can also become the basis for a much broader claim, and that claim gets repeated before the original information is checked.

A larger conclusion can organize scattered information and make a decision easier. It can also make a missing detail look irrelevant. Mercury in Sagittarius can explain what the information means, then overstate how much that information proves.
A complete answer can arrive too late for the conversation.
The discussion gets practical: What happens next, and who is responsible for it? Mercury in Capricorn organizes information into steps and keeps asking what a decision will require later.

Until {{exitDate}}, messages get edited down to the facts that affect the decision. In a meeting, someone turns a broad proposal into a sequence of steps and asks who is responsible for each one. A reply remains in drafts while someone considers what it could commit them to, and the person waiting for it starts treating the silence as a no.
Careful planning can clarify what happens next, but silence can make a practical concern sound like a refusal. Others may make the decision before the fuller explanation arrives.
The better idea still has to make sense to someone else.

Mercury in Aquarius notices the rule everyone keeps following and asks what problem it actually solves. A pattern across separate conversations can reveal a better method, but an explanation can be perfectly logical to its author and impossible for anyone else to use.

Until {{exitDate}}, a routine step gets questioned after someone notices it keeps creating the same delay. Separate messages reveal the same missing piece. An unfamiliar tool or method makes the next decision easier, while a meeting stalls because the person proposing it explains the entire system instead of answering the immediate question.

The idea may solve the larger problem and still leave the listener behind. If the explanation maps the whole system but never answers the immediate concern, a useful insight becomes difficult to act on.
Someone understands the message before they can explain how.

Mercury in Pisces hears hesitation in an agreeable reply and notices when a message leaves the central question unanswered. A conclusion can arrive through an image or association before the reasoning is clear enough for someone else to follow.

Until {{exitDate}}, someone hears uncertainty in a confident answer and realizes a decision is not settled. An image makes a difficult idea easier to understand than the formal explanation did. A plan becomes harder to carry out when the person who grasped it assumes everyone else made the same connection.

An impression may be accurate, but other people cannot act on an explanation they never heard. When the reasoning stays private, one person thinks the answer was obvious while everyone else makes decisions from incomplete information.
